YOUR UNIT, verbatim:
### U9b1c — Negotiate the MCP protocol version and refuse unbrokerable grants at compile

Ruling F1 of 2026-10-31 asked the controller to run a real Claude and a real Codex harness through a brokered launch under `no_new_privs` before U9b1b landed. The check, on a scratch realm copied from U9b1b's `enabled` fixture, found two defects that the fixture's deterministic harness cannot see, because it speaks MCP 2025-06-18 and reports success whatever the broker says.

(1) A real Claude seat holding the grant never reached its tools. Claude Code (2.1.3xx) opens with `initialize` asking protocol version 2025-11-25, and the broker refuses any version but its own (`crates/brokkr-cli/src/broker/rpc/calls.rs`, `Request::Initialize(id, _)` answering `Refused::Version`, -32602 "MCP protocol version is not supported by this broker", as MB3's text says). Claude Code then drops the server, and the seat runs without the tools it was granted. MCP 2025-06-18's lifecycle, which this design cites, says otherwise: "If the server supports the requested protocol version, it MUST respond with the same version. Otherwise, the server MUST respond with another protocol version it supports" (https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-06-18/basic/lifecycle). The broker now answers an `initialize` that asks any other version with its own 2025-06-18 result, and holds the session to 2025-06-18: a method that version does not admit still refuses "MCP method is not admitted by this broker", and every bound stays. An `initialize` whose `protocolVersion` is missing or not a string still refuses, with the existing cause. MB3's text in `specs/mcp-capability-broker/spec.md` says so. The controller's hand check: Claude Code asking 2025-11-25 accepted a stdio server that answered 2025-06-18, listed its tools and called one.

(2) A Codex seat holding a brokered grant compiled on Linux, then parked at dispatch with "broker ledger is missing for this attempt; the driver then failed: refusing to invoke the agent CLI: provider 'codex' has no measured strict MCP configuration for 'brokers'". By design (U7d), Codex's fragment and dsh's home carry no broker, so the driver always refuses a brokered set for them. The compile now refuses such a site with the driver's own cause, where the fence is lifted, so it fails at compile rather than after a dispatch. A provider whose fragment carries the broker (Claude) is unchanged.

(3) By the operator's ruling of 2026-10-31 ("B"), U9b1b landed by hand with task 46.1 open: its third review (M1) found the harness's death and the engine's timeout proved through real dispatch at every startup window but `Handoff`, which only the startup deadline ends. This unit proves both `Handoff` cases through real dispatch in `crates/brokkr-cli/tests/capability_broker/enabled/windows.rs`, establishing the delivered-frame, held-exec window (a store read alone does not establish it) and allowing for the tracer's delayed exec when bounding settlement: exact outcomes, teardown observations and a compiling removal each, then ticks 46.1.

Files: `crates/brokkr-cli/src/broker/rpc/calls.rs` and `crates/brokkr-cli/src/broker/rpc.rs`; `crates/brokkr-runtime/src/bundle/mcp.rs`, or the existing private child that holds the compile's strict check; `specs/mcp-capability-broker/spec.md` (MB3's text); `crates/brokkr-cli/tests/capability_broker/enabled/windows.rs` (item 3). New private children as the standing child-module rule allows, and their tests. No public API rise, and no edit to `crates/brokkr-protocol/src/adapters.rs`, `adapters/*.json` or `adapters/mcp/admit.rs`.

Closes tasks 46.3, 46.4 and 46.5, and 46.1's `Handoff` remainder; requirements [MB3](specs/mcp-capability-broker/spec.md), [SI2](specs/strict-mcp-isolation/spec.md), [MB5](specs/mcp-capability-broker/spec.md).
Proof: through the real binary, a harness asking 2025-11-25 is answered 2025-06-18, lists the granted tools and completes a call whose response is retained; one asking 2025-06-18 is unchanged; one that then calls a method 2025-06-18 does not admit is refused exactly; an `initialize` with no string version refuses as before. A Codex site and a dsh site holding a brokered grant refuse at compile with the driver's exact cause, and a Claude site still compiles. Independent compiling removals of the negotiation and of the compile refusal each fail their own test. At `Handoff`, the harness's death and the engine's timeout each end the attempt through real dispatch with their exact outcome, nothing left below the broker, and a compiling removal each. Host evidence, the controller's: a real Claude seat calls a granted tool through the broker and the call and its response are read back through `inspect --capability-call`.

Controller ruling 2026-10-31 (under the operator's standing ruling of 2026-10-28, the recommended options of the controller's real-harness check findings R1 and R2): both close in this small unit after U9b1b and before U9b2, whose guides then describe a grant a real Claude seat can use; any other file comes back to the operator. The holds of 2026-10-30 stand until this unit lands; by the operator's ruling of 2026-10-31, the release hold also waits for the boxed dsh hands fix, its own unit after U9b1b.

Owning tests: `crates/brokkr-cli/src/broker/rpc/tests.rs`, `crates/brokkr-cli/tests/capability_broker/enabled.rs` and its child modules, and the compile's MCP tests beside `crates/brokkr-runtime/src/bundle/mcp.rs`.

CONTROLLER'S STATE FOR U9b1c (the controller, 2026-10-31)

Your base is main with U9b1b merged. U9b1b's ruling F1 had the controller run a real Claude and a real Codex harness through a brokered launch before it landed. That check found the two defects this unit fixes. Its record is in .forge/u9b1c/: check-2026-10-31.md, Claude Code's own MCP logs for the run, the Codex park, and the script that built the scratch realm. Read it first. The design section "### U9b1c — " and tasks 46.3-46.5 are your scope. They arrive staged in your worktree.

1. R1, version negotiation. crates/brokkr-cli/src/broker/rpc/calls.rs answers `Request::Initialize(id, _)` for any version but 2025-06-18 with `Refused::Version`. Claude Code asks 2025-11-25, so it drops the server and the seat never sees its granted tools. Answer such an initialize with the broker's own 2025-06-18 result (the same greeting `greet` gives) and keep the session on 2025-06-18. Methods that version doesn't admit still refuse, and every bound stays. An initialize whose protocolVersion is missing or not a string still refuses with the existing cause. Fix MB3's text in specs/mcp-capability-broker/spec.md, which today says unknown versions refuse. Cite the lifecycle page the design cites. In the `enabled` suite, prove that a harness asking 2025-11-25 is answered 2025-06-18, lists the granted tools and completes a call whose response is retained. The suite's deterministic harness (`HARNESS` / `FRAMES` in crates/brokkr-cli/tests/capability_broker/enabled.rs) shows how. Record the compiling removal failing.
2. R2, compile refusal. A site holding a brokered grant on a provider whose fragment carries no broker (Codex, dsh) compiles today. It then parks at dispatch with "provider 'codex' has no measured strict MCP configuration for 'brokers'", raised by crates/brokkr-protocol/src/adapters/mcp.rs `isolated`. Refuse it at compile, where the fence is lifted, with that same cause, from the compile's strict check (crates/brokkr-runtime/src/bundle/mcp.rs or its existing private child). Don't edit adapters/mcp.rs, adapters.rs, adapters/*.json or adapters/mcp/admit.rs; read them only. A Claude site still compiles. Pin the Codex and dsh refusals exactly and record the compiling removal.
3. The Handoff window, task 46.5 (operator ruling 2026-10-31, "B"). U9b1b landed with task 46.1 open: its third review (M1) found that crates/brokkr-cli/tests/capability_broker/enabled/windows.rs ends every startup window three ways through real dispatch except `Handoff`, which only the startup deadline ends. Add the two missing cases there: hold a broker's startup at `Handoff` (the bootstrap's exec of the server delayed with the whole frame delivered and the status pipe open; a store read alone does not establish this window), then end it by the harness's death and, separately, by the engine's timeout of the attempt. Assert each exact outcome, `inspect`'s view, and that nothing stood below the broker remains; allow for the tracer's delayed exec when you bound settlement. Record a compiling removal and a restored pass for each, narrow windows.rs's module comment back to every window, tick 46.5 and 46.1, and update evidence/U9b1b.md's Tasks paragraph to say 46.1 closed here.
Already on your base, by the operator's rulings of 2026-11-01 (landed with U9b1b, after hosted merge-queue runners failed #933 on timing): windows.rs's teardown bounds are one `TEARDOWN` constant of 30 s, and the spent-share panel proof runs two members. Give your new Handoff cases the same `TEARDOWN`, and keep any new panel proof at two members or fewer (F8). No bound in the product moves; MB3's 30 s startup deadline stays as it is.
Make one signed commit (`git commit -S`) per item. Report `complete` when all three are proved, or `blocked` naming what is owed. Never report `oversized`.

Host evidence that isn't yours: the controller reruns the real Claude check on your tree. A real seat calls the granted tool through the broker, and the call is read back through `inspect --capability-call`. Record it as pending.

A fix anywhere else, or one that needs a public API rise, is a finding with options and your recommended one; don't make it. Already ruled; don't ask again: every ruling in design.md's U9b1, U9b1a, U9b1b and U9b1c sections. A boxed dsh hands seat refusing on Linux (#896) is a later unit's.

The holds stand until this unit lands: no house engine upgraded past U9b1a, no MCP grant in a house realm, and no release (by the operator's ruling of 2026-10-31 the release also waits for the boxed dsh hands fix, its own unit after U9b1b, not yours). None of them limits your test fixtures.

This seat may hold Claude's own web-search and web-fetch tools. Use them only for published sources (the MCP specification's lifecycle and versioning pages), and cite each URL you relied on in your notes.

STANDING RULINGS. Decision 0065's hold: off by default, no grandfathering; realm-only grants; tools are an abstraction, dialects the concrete; refuse, never reconcile (slice one's operator ruling of 2026-09-23). The MCP compile fence stays in place until U9b. Hosts are Linux and macOS only (decision 0063). Main's code-health rules bind: no `unsafe` in brokkr-runtime; `#[expect(.., reason)]`, never `#[allow]`; clippy's too_many_lines, excessive_nesting and struct_excessive_bools are denied, so split, and only if splitting would widen your unit carry `reason = "baseline 2026-09-29, decision 0065 slice one merged with main; split after #319"`; when a count moves, re-measure quality/'s file-lines, too-many-lines and suppressions (the steps quality/measure.sh uses), witness pins with `BROKKR_BLESS=1 cargo test -p brokkr-runtime --test witness_digests` (or, once #423's single test binary is on your base — crates/brokkr-runtime/tests/it.rs exists — `BROKKR_BLESS=1 cargo test -p brokkr-runtime --test it witness_digests::`), and budgets with scripts/measure-budgets.sh. Where a crate has tests/it.rs, a NEW tests/*.rs file must be registered as `mod <file>;` in that crate's tests/it.rs (layering::test_targets refuses an unregistered one), unless it sets HOME, cwd, env or a global allocator, in which case it is its own [[test]] in Cargo.toml with the reason written there; and `--test <file>` filters become `--test it <file>::` (capability_launch stays its own binary).

RULES. Touch at most the production files your row names; if the real scope exceeds them, STOP and report `oversized` with the split. One exception, the operator's standing rule of 2026-10-09 (operator-ruling-2026-10-03.md): beside a production file in your row that sits at its 800-line ceiling, or is frozen at its quality/file-lines.txt baseline above it, you may add NEW private child modules, declared from that file, in its own module tree and consumed in this unit, without stopping. The same holds beside a row file that your own change would push past 800 lines (extended 2026-10-11). You may also change an EXISTING private child module of a file in your row, in that file's own module tree (extended 2026-10-11). You may move existing code out of the full file into such a child to make room, preferring the code your change touches. Name each new file in your evidence and commit, and set its quality/file-lines.txt row. You may also add a name to an EXISTING re-export in the parent module that declares one of your row's files, where the parent's line count does not change (extended 2026-10-10). Files in any other module tree still mean `oversized`; any public API growth still needs the operator's ruling at PR time (record it, do not stop). Test files are NOT bounded by the row (controller's standing clarification, 2026-10-05): a test anywhere that pins behaviour your unit changes, a validator or fixture swap in another suite, or a new child test module beside an owning suite that sits over its line ceiling is part of your unit — size-neutral wherever a file sits at its quality/file-lines.txt baseline. A LOW finding you cannot fix inside your row's production files: record it in your result and do NOT report blocked for it. Tests assert exact reasons and values, never is_err(); every new test is bound by a compiling mutation that makes it fail, then restored, recorded (test, assertion) in evidence.md. Tick a task in tasks.md only on observed evidence; record results in a NEW file of your own, openspec/changes/decision-0065-capabilities-slice-two/evidence/U9b1c.md (two lanes deliver units at once, and every unit appending to evidence.md made each pair of pull requests conflict), and do not edit evidence.md itself; write it in prose or a table — never as a bullet list of the standard gate lines (`cargo fmt ...: clean`, `cargo clippy ...: clean`), which earlier evidence files already hold word for word, so the data clone gate refuses it; never edit the tasks.md preamble. Fixtures build on a canonicalised temporary root; no test reads .forge/ or needs an installed provider. Frozen contracts, policy/phase-machine.json, fixtures/, reference/ and extensions/ do not move unless your unit names them. Sign every commit (`git commit -S`; main requires signatures). HEADLESS SEAT: your session ends the moment you end a turn — never run a command in the background, never use Monitor or ScheduleWakeup, run every command in the foreground under the tool's 10-minute limit (suites crate by crate with `timeout 590`, split by --lib/--test if longer), and write your result file before you finish. GATES: cargo fmt --all -- --check; cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings; the suite of each crate you touched; openspec validate --all --strict; typos --hidden; git diff --check; quality/ratchet.sh files and clones. CI also builds and tests on macOS, which this host cannot: Linux-only code (namespaces, mountinfo, /proc, device numbers, Linux-only syscalls) goes behind `#[cfg(target_os = "linux")]` with a non-Linux stand-in that refuses, as broker/session.rs does, and any libc or rustix type you use must be the same type on both (rustix's Dev is u64 on Linux and i32 on macOS; U6c6a's first PR failed to compile there). Keep the session small; commit when the unit is done; never push.

house.content:
This realm is a Rust workspace. Production code is Rust under `crates/`; the
Rust-only architecture is recorded by decision 0009. Semantic changes carry a
decision document with status `proposed` because only the operator accepts one.
Intake seats read `README.md` and decisions 0004 and 0005 before framing a
commission, along with the code and history it touches.

The frozen v1 contracts under `contracts/`, the production table at
`policy/phase-machine.json`, and `reference/` (its schemas included) are
read-only.
A contract change lands as a new version file beside the old one, never as an
edit. The evaluator corpus under `fixtures/` is also frozen and is never
regenerated, only versioned.

Tests are part of every change. Extend the suite that proves the code, run
`cargo test --workspace`, compile `recipes/self`, and leave formatting, clippy,
and the exact-coverage gate clean before reporting success.

Commit completed work with `git` using the repository's message style. Never
push.

The supported hosts are Linux and macOS (decision 0063); WSL2 is Linux. Write
no Windows-conditional code, test or evidence.

## Architecture

Decision 0071 rules how code here is shaped. Build to it, and cite its ruling
numbers in what you judge. Where a gate named below holds a rule, the gate is
the authority, and a finding it would catch is the gate's.

- **Pure core (ruling 1).** `brokkr-core` and `brokkr-view` do no I/O and read
  no clock, environment or randomness. They run no process. Pass `now`, paths
  and environment in as arguments. Effects live in the crates above core and
  view, and are journaled.
- **Enums and data, not traits (ruling 2).** A closed set is an enum matched
  exhaustively, with no wildcard arm that decides behaviour. Anything an
  operator extends is data under `adapters/`, `agents/`, `recipes/` or
  `realms.json`, validated and digested. Add a trait only for a seam whose
  contract spans several operations that must stay consistent with one
  another, reached across a process or service boundary, and name that seam
  in its doc comment. `ProducerTransport` is the one such trait today. A test
  double alone does not make a seam: a single substitutable function is a
  closure seam (`*_with`, `*_in`), which is how the house inverts a
  dependency otherwise.
- **Typed at the edge (ruling 3).** Parse wire, file and harness data once
  into a type, with `serde` and `deny_unknown_fields` where the contract is
  closed. `serde_json::Value` never goes past the edge, into state, or back
  out by string key. Never put `format!("{:?}")` in anything digested or
  journaled. A doubly-optional field or a string vocabulary is a missing enum.
- **Small functions (ruling 4).** New and changed functions stay within 100
  lines, nesting depth 5 and 7 parameters. Cyclomatic complexity follows
  the operator's 2026-09-26 ruling: a function may reach the higher of 15
  and its baseline, so a new function stays within 15, an existing one may
  change freely up to 15, and one already over 15 may only shrink.
  Production files stay within 800 lines and test files within 2,000, and a
  file already over may not grow. Add no new `jscpd` clone in production
  code, test code or data. `quality/` holds the measured baseline. Today's
  offenders carry `#[allow(clippy::…)]`, and #337 converts them to
  `#[expect(clippy::…, reason = "…")]`. Add a suppression only by a ruling,
  and remove it when you fix the function. A new suppression is
  `#[expect(…, reason)]`, never `#[allow]`.
- **Once (ruling 5).** Every fact has one home. A repeated vocabulary, skeleton
  or helper becomes one function or one table. An agent is defined once under
  `agents/`, and seats hire it by reference. A recipe that differs from another
  by a model, a seat or an entry is an `extends` overlay, never a copy. The
  agent library does not yet accept `extends`, and #360 builds it. Until then,
  a variation of an agent lives at the seat that hires it, overridden in a
  recipe overlay. It is never a second agent file that restates the first. A
  copy that must exist, such as a script a bundle pins, is held to its source
  by a test.
- **Nothing unused (ruling 6).** Add no alias, agent, contract version, flag or
  `pub` item without a consumer, and prefer `pub(crate)`. A deprecation names
  the release that removes it.
- **One derivation (ruling 7).** A fact shown on two surfaces is derived once
  in `brokkr-view`. The CLI, the TUI and `ui.html` only paint it. The engine
  never admits anything by a display-crate function.
- **Typed errors (ruling 8).** Return a `thiserror` enum whose `Display` keeps
  the operator's text. Tests match variants and pin each module's text once.
  Add no new `Result<_, String>`.
- **Tests that bind (ruling 9).** Assert exact values or variants, never
  `is_err()` alone. Show that every new test binds: a compiling mutation that
  removes the behaviour must make it fail. Restore the behaviour and record
  the failing test. Share fixtures through builders. Never change the process
  environment without a guard that restores it on unwind. A production guard
  left out because the exact-coverage gate would count it unreachable carries
  a removal-control test for the invariant that makes it unreachable, and the
  comment explaining the omission names that test.
- **The house's patterns (ruling 10).**
  - A harness is a module behind `AdapterKind`. This is the target form;
    today all five kinds share one module, and #347 and #348 build the
    split.
  - A CLI verb is a `Cmd` variant plus a handler.
  - A long parameter list becomes a parameter object.
  - Argv and mount tables are built with a builder.
  - Observing the world is split from deciding on it.
  - Never use a trait-object registry for a closed set.

Judges rate a finding against these rulings by this table, and cite the ruling
number:

- **info:** something a house gate would catch. The gate's verdict is the
  authority.
- **low:** a new or changed function over a ceiling, a rule written a second
  time, an item added without a consumer, or a `Value` carried past its edge
  within one module.
- **medium:** an untyped vocabulary that crosses crates, recipe or agent data
  copied instead of extended, a fact derived a second time on another surface,
  an error matched by its text, or a new test that cannot fail.
- **high or above:** any violation that hides a fail-open path or weakens a
  refusal. It is carried as a security finding.

A principle the implementer bent knowingly, and named with its reason in
`notes`, is still rated, and the judge carries that reason with the finding.

## Release configuration

The release manager prepares the candidate and profile patches; the operator
publishes them. Local validation is preparation work. Remote CI on the final PR
head, publication, channel updates and live-profile verification are handoff
steps, recorded as pending until their remote results exist. Historical
"live from" channel versions and old journal examples are historical facts,
not current-version references to replace.

```json
{
  "repository": "feedback-loop-ai/brokkr",
  "default_branch": "main",
  "tag_format": "v{version}",
  "version_files": ["Cargo.toml", "Cargo.lock"],
  "version_update": "Bump the workspace package and six path-dependency versions together. Run cargo update --workspace --offline without upgrading registry dependencies. Measure and update the witness and compose manifest digests because the engine version participates in their identity.",
  "release_notes": "docs/releases/v{version}.md",
  "handoff_directory": "docs/releases/v{version}",
  "scratch_directory": ".forge/release",
  "documentation": ["README.md", "ARCHITECTURE.md", "CONTRIBUTING.md", "docs/guides/", "packaging/README.md"],
  "validation": [
    {"name": "format", "command": "cargo fmt --all -- --check"},
    {"name": "clippy", "command": "cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings"},
    {"name": "tests", "command": "cargo test --workspace --all-features --locked"},
    {"name": "self bundle", "command": "cargo run --locked -p brokkr-cli -- compile --bundle recipes/self"},
    {"name": "verify bundle", "command": "cargo run --locked -p brokkr-cli -- compile --bundle recipes/verify"},
    {"name": "exact coverage", "instructions": "Run bash scripts/coverage-exact.sh in CI or host validation outside the workspace box before tagging. Boundary tests require creating a namespace, which the box deliberately refuses to nest. Record this check as pending in the preparation handoff until that external result exists; never lower the coverage gate."},
    {"name": "release binary", "command": "cargo build --release --locked -p brokkr-cli"},
    {"name": "remote CI", "instructions": "Before tagging, require all applicable CI jobs on the final candidate commit, including both supported operating systems, MSRV, licenses, audit, packaging and exact coverage."}
  ],

  ],
  "channels": [
    {"name": "GitHub release", "evidence": "Four platform archives, Linux deb/rpm packages, SHA256SUMS and signed build provenance."},
    {"name": "crates.io", "evidence": "All seven workspace crates serve the new version."},
    {"name": "apt and rpm", "evidence": "The signed Pages repositories index the new packages."},
    {"name": "Homebrew and Nix", "evidence": "The generated channel PRs are merged and their versions and digests match the release manifest."}
  ],
  "extensions": [

    {"name": "frozen contracts", "instructions": "Compare contracts, fixtures, policy/phase-machine.json and reference against the previous release; explain additive versions and flag modifications to frozen bytes.", "evidence": "A reviewed diff with migration notes for any new contract versions."}
```
